title: Infra: GPU Fleet, Cloud Accounts & IaC CI/CD Runbook
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview
========
This runbook consolidates infrastructure engineering guidance for Redwood's GPU fleet and capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking baseline, Terraform/IaC module patterns, and CI/CD/build pipelines. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for GPU-backed inference capacity across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope
-----
- GPU fleet capacity planning and autoscaling guidelines (multi-region)
- Cloud accounts & networking baseline for inference clusters
- Recommended Terraform/IaC module interfaces and patterns
- CI/CD pipeline structure for module builds, tests, and deployments
- Runbook steps for common operational incidents (capacity, networking, CI failures)

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
- Primary: Infra-GPU team (owner: @infra-gpu)
- Secondary: Infra-Platform (networking, cloud accounts)
- On-call: infra-gpu rotation (see /oncall-and-incident-response)
- Pager escalation: infra-sre -> infra-platform -> eng-leads (pager duty escalation policy)

SLOs and Capacity Targets
-------------------------
- Target average GPU utilization: 60% (capacity planning target).
- Avoid sustained utilization > 80% for more than 10 minutes.
- Headroom reserve: 20% of cluster capacity per region to absorb bursts and failover.
- P99 request-start latency SLO (from API gateway to container start/kickoff): < 250 ms for hot instances, < 5s for cold starts.
- Pod queue length threshold for autoscaling decisions: scale when avg queue length > 4 per GPU for > 3 minutes.

Fleet Sizing Methodology (step-by-step)
-------------------------------------
1. Collect qps and tokens-per-request metrics by route and model variant for a 30-day window.
2. Convert to effective GPU-seconds using per-model perf profiles (tokens/sec per GPU, memory footprint).
3. Set safety headroom = max(20% of required GPUs, 3 GPUs).
4. Allocate per-region capacity proportional to observed regional demand + recovery reserve for region failover.
5. Run autoscaling policy simulation with 95th percentile traffic spikes (use the capacity-sim tool).
6. Approve changes via PR to infra capacity repo; include cost delta and rollback plan.

Autoscaling and Policies
------------------------
- Horizontal scale: add/remove worker instances (container tasks) mapped to individual GPUs.
- Scale-up triggers (OR):
  - avg queue length > 4 per GPU for 3m
  - 95th percentile GPU utilization > 85% for 5m
  - Pod OOM events or GPU memory pressure > 90%
- Scale-down guardrails:
  - Minimum stable period: 10 minutes after scale-up before allowing scale-down
  - Do not scale down below committed capacity or reserved headroom
- Burst capacity: allow ephemeral burst pool in Dedicated deployments up to 15% over committed for 10 minutes; billing signal generated for accounting.

Cloud Accounts & Networking Baseline
-----------------------------------
- Account model: one management account + per-region inference accounts (AWS orgs / projects).
- Networking: each inference account has a single VPC per region with standardized CIDR allocation (10.20.X.0/22 pattern).
- Subnets: private-worker-subnet, control-subnet, optional public-egress-subnet.
- Security groups: least-privilege rules; worker SGs only allow egress to model-store endpoints and control-plane endpoints on required ports.
- Cross-account access: use IAM roles with short-lived credentials; VPC endpoints for S3 and internal services.
- Peering and Transit: use Transit Gateway for multi-account peering where low-latency cross-region replication or KV-cache sync is required.

Terraform / IaC Module Patterns
------------------------------
Design goals: idempotent, testable modules with clear interfaces and separation of concerns.
Required module categories:
- accounts (create organization-level accounts and baseline resources)
- vpc (VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT/egress)
- compute-gpu (instance profiles, ASG/ECS nodegroup, kube labels for GPU type)
- iam (roles/policies for workers, control plane, observability)
- networking-helpers (vpc endpoints, transit gateway attachments)
- ci-cd (pipelines and module release orchestration)

Module interface example (compute-gpu):
- variables: gpu_type, min_capacity, max_capacity, instance_profile_arn, subnet_ids, ami_id, node_labels, gpu_count_per_node
- outputs: autoscaling_group_id, instance_role_arn, nodegroup_name, security_group_id

Recommended practices:
- Keep modules small and composable (single responsibility).
- Use automated module linting (tflint) and tfsec security scans in PRs.
- Publish module versions to the internal module registry with CHANGELOG and upgrade notes.
- Provide acceptance tests that deploy a minimal stack into a disposable account and run smoke inference workloads.

CI/CD and Build Pipelines
-------------------------
Pipeline layout:
1. terraform-modules pipeline (push to main triggers):
   - syntax/lint (tflint, terrascan)
   - unit tests (terraform-compliance rules)
   - plan under a disposable workspace (use ephemeral cloud account)
   - run acceptance suite (deploy minimal cluster + smoke tests)
   - publish module artifact to registry on success
2. infra-deploy pipeline (applies changes to live accounts):
   - change review + cost estimate step (terraform-cost-estimator)
   - gated by approvers list (owners and finance for capacity changes)
   - apply via ephemeral runner with short-lived creds
3. compute image pipeline (GPU AMI builds):
   - base image build (packer) -> artifactify -> security scan -> publish to AMI catalog

CI Best Practices:
- Every change to compute-gpu module must include an acceptance test that runs a representative ML workload for 5 minutes.
- Changes that may impact capacity (min_capacity, max_capacity, autoscaler strategies) must attach a capacity simulation output to the PR.
- Do not allow direct TF state manipulation; all modifications must go through pipelines.

Runbooks: Incidents & Playbooks
------------------------------
1) Capacity shortage (symptoms: sudden elevated queue length, high rejection/429s, P99 latency spike)\   Steps:
   - Triage: check cluster dashboard (GPU utilization, queue length, node count)
   - If autoscaler is not reacting: inspect autoscaler logs, controller manager, and AWS ASG/ECS metrics
   - If cluster saturated and autoscaling healthy: initiate emergency scale-up via infra-deploy pipeline to add 2x headroom or enable burst pool
   - If new nodes failing to join: check AMI compatibility, kubelet logs, IAM profile, and security group egress
   - Postmortem: create incident in incidents tracker, capture root cause, and schedule capacity increase or code fixes

2) Networking / cross-account failure (symptoms: model store access errors, S3 access timeouts, KV-cache partition)\   Steps:
   - Verify VPC endpoints and route tables in the affected account
   - Check IAM role assume logs and STS failures
   - Confirm Transit Gateway attachments state for cross-account routes
   - If DNS resolution failing: verify Route53 resolver endpoints and conditional forwarders
   - Remediation: failover to regional replica or toggle control-plane fallback routing; escalate to infra-platform if Transit/GW changes required

3) CI/CD pipeline failure on module push\   Steps:
   - Inspect pipeline logs (lint, unit tests, acceptance) and reproduce locally using the same TF/TFLint versions
   - If lint/scan failure: fix code or update policies in central lint config; re-run commit in a new branch
   - If acceptance tests failing: run smoke test harness and capture failure traces; revert on master if publish already occurred and rollback module version in registry

Operational Notes and Guardrails
-------------------------------
- Cost checkpoints: any capacity change > $5k/month requires finance review and explicit approval.
- Change windows: large capacity migrations or multi-region failovers should be scheduled in maintenance windows (weekend nights 00:00-04:00 PT) unless emergency.
- Security scans: all module releases must pass tfsec and image scanning before reaching production.
- Tagging policy: resources must include tags: service, team, env, cost-center, infra-owner.

Appendix: Useful commands and examples
-------------------------------------
- Terraform plan in disposable workspace:
  TF_VAR_org_account=ephemeral-123 hack/ci/terraform-plan.sh --workspace ephemeral-123

- Simulate autoscaler behavior (local):
  python tools/capacity_sim.py --traffic-file examples/95pct_spike.json --perf-profile models/llama-2-7b.json --headroom 0.2

- Sample compute-gpu module variables (HCL excerpt):
  module "compute_gpu" {
    source = "github.com/redwood-infra/modules/compute-gpu"
    gpu_type = "nvidia-a100-80gb"
    min_capacity = 4
    max_capacity = 200
    gpu_count_per_node = 1
    subnet_ids = var.worker_subnet_ids
    instance_profile_arn = aws_iam_instance_profile.gpu_workers.arn
  }
